title: ECNEC approves Tk 33,298 crore in projects, including canal digging
excerpt: Almost all the money is from the government's own budget. Projects cover canals in 64 districts, river erosion, rural roads and a livelihood programme.
content:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday (18 November) approved 16 projects with a combined cost of Tk 33,298.48 crore, Bangladesh Post reported, citing BSS. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman chaired the meeting. Fourteen projects are new and two are revisions.

The government will pay Tk 32,863.76 crore from its own funds. Project loans make up Tk 424.73 crore, and the implementing agencies will put in Tk 10 crore. State Minister for Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki briefed reporters after the meeting.

What was approved

  • A nationwide project to re-excavate canals, small rivers and water bodies
  • River erosion protection in Jamalpur and Barishal
  • Rural infrastructure in several districts
  • A revised third phase of the Rural Livelihood Project
  • Small-scale irrigation in Joypurhat, Bogura and Gaibandha

Before the meeting, The Financial Express reported that the canal project would cost Tk 69.22 billion, be run by the Bangladesh Water Development Board, and cover about 8,898 km of waterways in all 64 districts, with about 107,000 trees to be planted. It is linked to the governing BNP's pledge to dig 20,000 km of canals.

Why it matters

These are large, mostly home-funded commitments in water management, flood control and rural livelihoods, where many NGOs work with local communities. Canal digging can ease waterlogging and support irrigation, but it can also displace people who live or farm on canal land, so community consultation and fair compensation will matter.

What to watch

How quickly money is released for these projects, and how the canal work handles people living along the banks.
